processes.description: The validation group questions monthly forward gas curves whose shape or level moved sharply. Darron Giron forwards the flagged curves to the traders asking them to identify the factors driving the change, chases when no answer comes, and relays the explanation back: that Phillip Allen and Keith Holst confirmed the curve changes in question, or that the market simply traded higher in the West during the month.
steps: The validation group flags forward gas curves whose shape or level changed drastically.
Darron Giron forwards the flagged curves to the trading group and asks what is driving the change.
If no answer arrives, he asks anyone in the group to follow up on the curves.
Traders explain the move, such as the market trading higher in the West.
The explanation is relayed back to the validation group.

stalls.summary: Flagged curves wait on the traders to explain them: the request to identify the drivers of a drastic change had to be followed by a second ask for anyone in the group to follow up.

automation.approach: A monthly curve-change report that compares each forward gas curve with the prior month's mark, flags large shape or level moves by location and month, and keeps a log where traders record the reason for each flagged move, so the validation group receives the flags with the market explanation already attached.
automation.rationale: The round is a question-and-answer loop between validation and the desk, and the answers are short market explanations that recur. A standard curve-change explanation log removes the forward-and-wait step and gives the validation group one place to read the reasons.

processes.description: Coordinators, mainly Heather Choate, organize customer trips, the annual Enron Customer Meeting and customer happy hours. A round starts with a trip proposal or a planning notice, then invitations go out as attachments, hosts are asked to confirm their customers or name replacements by a deadline (Friday, June 29, 2001 by 12pm), a final guest list with activities is circulated for review, and the schedule is revised and redistributed when attendees change.
steps: The coordinator drafts the customer trip or meeting proposal and circulates it.
Planning starts and invitations are prepared and sent to hosts and customers.
Hosts confirm their customers or name replacements by the stated deadline.
The coordinator compiles the final guest list with activities, rooming and itinerary.
The final list and schedule are distributed for review and staff mark their calendars.
The schedule is revised and redistributed when attendees change.

stalls.summary: Guest lists and schedules change late in a round: hosts replacing customers are given a hard deadline to say so, and a trip schedule had to be revised and redistributed after a change in who was attending.

automation.approach: A shared event workbook per round holding the guest list, RSVPs, replacements, activities and rooming, from which the final guest list and itinerary are produced, plus standard invitation, reminder and replacement-deadline messages reused across trips, meetings and happy hours.
automation.rationale: Most of the hands-on work is keeping guest lists, activities and rooming lists consistent as people confirm or swap out, and rebuilding the schedule when they do. A single guest-list and itinerary layout lets the coordinator update one source and regenerate the distributed lists instead of reworking them by hand.

work_estimate.rationale: Rounds range from a happy hour notice (about 20 minutes to set up) to a customer trip or annual meeting, where drafting the proposal, preparing invitations, tracking confirmations and replacements, and compiling the final guest list with activities and rooming takes several hours; 90 minutes is a middle round. Tracking RSVPs and regenerating lists and schedules is the part a template and tracker could take over; choosing guests and activities stays with people.

processes.description: Originators and marketers work customer leads and opportunities: a lead or product pitch is forwarded with a question about interest, meetings are arranged to discuss gas supply opportunities, customers ask for historical data for 1999 and 2000 before a meeting, staff estimate a prospect's energy requirements from published articles, contact reports are passed on after calls, and analysts are assigned to compile regional supply, market and infrastructure analysis. Existing relationships are checked by asking whether anyone has contacted the customer about renewing.
steps: A lead, product pitch or customer contact arrives and is forwarded to an originator.
The originator decides whether to pursue it and arranges a meeting with the customer.
Market or historical data the customer asked for is gathered before the meeting.
Supporting analysis is prepared, such as estimating a prospect's energy requirements from published sources.
After the call or meeting, a contact report is written and shared.
Renewals of existing customer relationships are followed up.

stalls.summary: Leads and renewals lack a clear owner: a renewal with an existing customer is raised by asking whether anyone has contacted them, and leads are passed along asking who is interested.

automation.approach: A shared lead and contact log recording each lead, its owner, the meeting date, the data the customer asked for and the contact report, with renewal dates for existing customers flagged ahead of time, plus a standard pre-meeting data pack drawn from existing fundamentals and market data.
automation.rationale: The recurring work is gathering customer data, preparing for meetings and recording what was said, and the stalls come from leads and renewals with no named owner. A common contact-report and lead-tracker layout makes ownership visible and lets data pulls be reused across customers.

work_estimate.rationale: The minutes go to pulling historical or market data a customer requested, estimating a prospect's energy needs from outside sources, preparing for the meeting and writing the contact report afterwards. A simple forwarded lead takes little; a prepared customer meeting with a data request takes a couple of hours, so 45 minutes is a typical round. Standard data pulls and report layouts can be automated; judging the opportunity and talking to the customer cannot.
